title: Word-position conditioning fails to improve fresh paired controls and exposes boundary artifacts
statement: I preregistered two role-correct position-conditioned variants of the bilateral context loss, froze their cutoffs before evaluation, and tested new contrasts and text windows. On the same thirty supported full-coverage matched-left evaluation repeats, unconditioned bilateral JS ranks genuine candidates first in 30/30, while both position variants do so in 27/30. The informative-direction cutoff accepts 7 genuine candidates and 7 decoys. Position conditioning leaves the old us/um reversal in four of five repeats. Negative direct-emission controls produce more acceptances with the position variants, including on the all-method common-supported subset. An inclusive boundary score also accepts a standalone-letter synthetic counterexample at zero loss; the informative variant abstains. This is a negative result for the specified refinement; no manuscript candidate was evaluated.
check: At the recorded runtime base, reproduce calibration, evaluation and the independent role-table/entropy audit with the embedded runner. Verify public pre-analysis and cutoff commits, exact file digests, support/abstention counts, primary comparisons and no-fusion controls. The tested word-position refinement should not be deployed as evidence of glyph composition. A next investigation should distinguish pair-specific lexical/morphological contexts from component contexts on fresh books, with sensitivity and specificity fixed before manuscript use.

plan.hypothesis: Role-correct start/middle/end conditioning improves the bilateral context test on new contrasts and reduces deterministic-boundary artifacts.

scores.unconditioned: (JS(prev(C),prev(A))+JS(next(C),next(B)))/2, identical definition to previous bilateral JS.
scores.position_all: For each C stratum (initial I, final F), compare prev(C|I,F) to prev(A|I,not-final) and next(C|I,F) to next(B|not-initial,F); average the two JS divergences and weight by C stratum counts.
scores.position_info: Use the same strata and role-correct references, but exclude deterministic left contexts when C is initial and right contexts when C is final. Sum count-weighted informative-direction JS values and divide by the count-weighted number of informative directions. A candidate occurring only as a one-letter word has no informative direction and is unscorable.

plan.js: Equal-weight Jensen-Shannon divergence, base-2 logarithms, zero terms omitted, no smoothing. Each word has explicit virtual space boundaries. All streams use single spaces.
plan.eligibility: Candidate and each component count >=40. For each conditional reference actually used, require >=20 occurrences in that reference position class. position_info additionally requires >=40 candidate occurrences with at least one informative direction. Unsupported scores are None, reported as abstentions. Primary paired comparisons and calibration use cases where all three scores are available for both X and Z.
plan.windows: Normalize with pinned refcorpus. Calibration: calib_text from character 40000 onward. Evaluation: control_text from character 80000 onward. Training negative chains: train_text from character 40000 onward. Drop the leading partial word after the offset, take up to 40000 characters, drop the last partial word, and surround with spaces. Remaining evaluation text is shorter for Latin and Italian; report length and exclusions without length tuning.
plan.pairing: Match target AB and decoy AD by word-initial/word-final flags. Modes slots, left (also previous glyph), both (also previous and next glyph). Shuffle occurrence lists per group, pair them, exclude edits with start distance <3 or within 2 positions of an earlier accepted start, then shuffle accepted pairs. Replace targets by X and decoys by Z in the same stream.
plan.decision: Lower loss wins; differences <=1e-12 are ties. Seeds reuse the same source and are robustness repeats, not independent evidence units. Report all six contrasts separately.
plan.threshold: For each score, pool common-eligible primary calibration Z losses, sort n values, and choose zero-based order statistic floor(0.05*n). Accept strictly below cutoff-1e-12. Publish cutoffs and their file hash before any evaluation outcomes. If n=0, report unavailable, with no replacement threshold.
plan.diagnostics: Separate from primary calibration: evaluate us/um on the old Latin evaluation window (control offset40000) using old seeds58471,58477,58481,58487,58493, left/full coverage, and on the new Latin evaluation window using the new seed list. The old window is already exposed and cannot provide independent validation. Its old expected source SHA256 is b16a76590cd083c88a3e94d7c41a9a7102ff20a78e92848a7ec25d61acb1fa93.
plan.negative_controls: Score every lower-case candidate C distinct from A and B, count>=40, for every fixed primary component pair on untouched evaluation streams and 20 new direct-emission first-order chains per language. Fit a shared character transition table on the specified fresh training window; sample starts from word starts, forbid final space, generate len(evaluation_source)-2 characters and wrap in spaces. Report accepted/supported/abstained candidate counts by method, and stream-level any acceptance, plus the all-method common-supported subset.
plan.structural_checks: Verify JS entropy identity, reversal with swapped A/B, equal input-context ties, and the one-letter-word boundary trap using synthetic x/ab/aba/bab words. position_all must score a standalone x as zero if references exist; position_info must abstain. Record whether frozen thresholds accept that zero, without changing the rule.
plan.manuscript_gate: No manuscript candidate triplets will be evaluated; selected reference controls do not settle glyph composition.
plan.stop_rule: No contrast, weight, seed, support, window, threshold or matching changes after outcomes. Bugs require a documented amendment and new plan hash.

scripts.reproduce.py:
"""Run from the recorded repository base: python reproduce.py STEP_JSON SCRATCH."""
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys

submission = json.loads(Path(sys.argv[1]).read_bytes())
scratch = Path(sys.argv[2]).resolve()
scratch.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
for record in submission['input_files']:
    data = Path(record['file']).read_bytes()
    if record.get('hash_mode') == 'lf_normalized':
        data = data.replace(b'\r\n', b'\n')
    assert hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest() == record['sha256'], record['file']
(scratch/'plan.json').write_bytes(submission['reproduction']['plan_json_bytes'].encode())
for name, code in submission['reproduction']['scripts'].items():
    (scratch/name).write_bytes(code.encode())
environment = dict(os.environ)
environment['PYTHONPATH'] = str(Path.cwd())+os.pathsep+environment.get('PYTHONPATH', '')
def verify(name):
    assert hashlib.sha256((scratch/name).read_bytes()).hexdigest() == submission['output_digests'][name], name
for name in ('plan.json', 'position_context.py'):
    verify(name)
for command, output in [(['position_context.py', 'calibrate'], 'calibration.json'),
                         (['position_context.py', 'evaluate'], 'evaluation.json'),
                         (['verify_position.py'], 'verification.json')]:
    subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-X', 'utf8', str(scratch/command[0]), *command[1:]],
                   env=environment, check=True, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    verify(output)
    print(output, 'exact digest matched', flush=True)

reproduction.instructions: Use the repository at runtime_base with verified pinned reference files. Extract reproduce.py from the scripts dictionary. From the repository root run python reproduce.py /path/to/step.json /path/to/scratch. The runner checks input hashes, saves exact embedded plan/script bytes, runs calibration then evaluation and independent verification, and verifies exact output digests. All outputs use explicit UTF-8 bytes and LF across platforms. Full negative-candidate tables are recreated in evaluation.json; the submission retains all paired rows, every negative sample minimum/acceptance list, support counts and aggregate common-support comparisons.

findings: The protocol and executable were published in ee8f347 before outcomes; calibration cutoffs were published in 7ca696c before evaluation. No planned contrast, support, weight, seed, window or cutoff rule was retuned. The runtime uses upstream base recorded in runtime_base; the data publication branch uses an older fork ancestor and adds only this experiment directory.

Role mapping: a candidate at initial/final flags I,F is compared on the left with A at I,not-final and on the right with B at not-initial,F. Inclusive scores average both directions by candidate-stratum counts. The informative variant drops deterministic initial-left and final-right boundary directions and requires forty informative candidate occurrences.

Primary calibration has 25 common-supported cases out of 30 attempts. At the frozen order-statistic cutoffs, unconditioned JS accepts 17 genuine candidates and 1 decoy, inclusive position JS 15 and 1, and informative position JS 10 and 1. Informative positioning supports all thirty calibration pairs individually, but the shared comparison/calibration subset excludes five unsupported inclusive-position cases by the frozen plan.

Primary evaluation has all thirty pairs supported by all methods. Unconditioned bilateral JS gives thirty genuine wins; both position variants give twenty-seven wins and three decoy wins. All three position-related reversals occur in the Latin in/is contrast: position variants win two of five repeats; all five other contrasts win five of five repeats. These are six contrast/text strata with five related seed repetitions each, not thirty independent language samples.

Frozen primary evaluation cutoff decisions: unconditioned accepts 20 genuine/4 decoy; inclusive position accepts 15 genuine/3 decoy; informative position accepts 7 genuine/7 decoy. Calibration decoy acceptance does not transfer as a universal five-percent error rate.

With word-position flags matched but previous glyph not matched, evaluation full-coverage genuine wins are 24/30 unconditioned versus 19/30 under either position variant. Under full matching of both neighboring contexts, every common-supported pair ties as expected; only 10/30 full-coverage cases meet all support rules and 5/30 half-coverage cases do so. Exclusions are retained.

The exposed old us/um evaluation window exactly reproduces all five prior unconditioned bilateral scores and its five decoy wins. Both position variants change only one of those five to a genuine win, leaving four reversals. On the fresh later Latin window all three methods win five of five. This diagnostic does not validate a repair on independent data; the old window was already exposed and the new-window baseline already succeeds.

Among natural no-fusion controls, the all-method common-supported subset contains 105 combinations: unconditioned accepts 4, inclusive position 12, informative position 4. Among sixty new direct-emission streams the common subset has 1985 combinations: acceptance counts are 71 unconditioned, 221 inclusive position, and 115 informative position. All-support counts and abstentions are also recorded; conditioned support exclusions are not counted as correct rejections.

The preregistered synthetic stream repeating x ab aba bab a hundred times supplies both reference component positions but x is always a whole word. Inclusive position scoring returns loss zero and accepts x as an ab candidate under the frozen cutoff. The informative variant has no informative direction and abstains, as required by its definition.

Independent regex/event extraction, explicit four-case role mapping and entropy-form JS verify 2220 paired score values and 7164 negative-control score values including abstentions. All support and cutoff decisions match; maximum numerical discrepancy is 6.661338147750939e-16. Independently sampled negative streams reproduce all 63 natural/generated source hashes.
limitations: Only normalized public reference texts and controlled substitutions were used. No manuscript signs, hidden pages or glyph images were tested.
Six selected contrasts and three pinned languages do not establish a universal ranking of methods. Repeated seeds share text and replacement pools.

Fresh calibration and evaluation windows are disjoint from earlier used prefixes, but they come from the same pinned books. Remaining Latin and Italian evaluation windows are shorter; support exclusions are reported without changing the planned window or minimum counts.

Pooling related calibration negatives does not guarantee a population error rate. All compared cutoffs are method-specific and frozen; changes in sensitivity or false acceptance cannot be interpreted without those operating points.

Role-correct position conditioning still compares residual components with pair-specific contexts; grammar, vocabulary and partial substitution remain confounders. The negative result applies to the specified coarse position variants, not every possible positional model.

The us/um old-window result is an exposed diagnostic, excluded from calibration and primary evidence. The single-word boundary trap is a structural counterexample, not an empirical estimate of its prevalence.
